children: New Zealand's consumer confidence rebounded in November to its highest level since January, as shoppers grew more upbeat on the back of falling fuel prices at the pump, ANZ-Roy Morgan data showed on Friday.

The consumer confidence index rose to 100.2 in November, up from 96.2 in October, as two-year inflation expectations eased to their lowest level in nearly two years. A reading above 100 indicates optimism, while a reading below 100 signals pessimism.

"Consumers (are) feeling more chipper about their future prospects than their current circumstances. Still, it was good to see both the current and future conditions indexes rise this month," the survey said.
